[[File:Roger Hendrix at 2011 ASM General Meeting.jpg|thumb|Hendrix at the 2011 [[American Society for Microbiology]] General Meeting in New Orleans.]]
'''Roger W. Hendrix''' (July 7, 1943 – August 15, 2017) was an American biologist, focusing in bacteriophage biology, and a distinguished professor at [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref name="obit" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.biology.pitt.edu/person/roger-hendrix |title=Roger Hendrix |publisher=pitt.edu |accessdate=May 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/science/2009/04/06/The-Thinkers-Tiny-viruses-that-infect-bacteria-affect-our-health/stories/200904060189 |title=The Thinkers |date=April 6, 2009 |publisher=post-gazette.com |access-date=May 13, 2017}}</ref> He studied biology at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and went on to obtain his Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of [[James Watson]], the co-discoverer of the structure of [[DNA]].<ref name="obit">{{Cite web |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/obituaries/2017/09/05/Obituary-Roger-W-Hendrix-university-of-pittsburgh-molecular-biology-and-renaissance-music/stories/201709050012 |title=Obituary: Roger W. Hendrix / Lover of molecular biology and Renaissance music |date=5 September 2017 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref> In 2009, he received the [[NAS Award for Scientific Reviewing]].

He died on August 15, 2017.<ref name="obit" />
